# GEO report: harbor-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 63/100, Needs work

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 15.67 ÷ 25 × 100 = 63. High = (15.67 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 63.

The site is a small Astro site that renders to plain HTML, so the basics are readable. Four problems cost points. Two AI search crawlers are blocked, every page names the home page as its canonical, both structured-data blocks are broken, and a site-wide snippet limit is set. Nothing is unknown, so the score is a single number. These results are read from code, not measured on a live site.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Let the AI search crawlers in (or confirm that blocking them is deliberate)
- **Why it matters:** `OAI-SearchBot` (ChatGPT search) and `PerplexityBot` are told to stay out of the whole site. Those tools can't read your pages to answer questions.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4-8`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: OAI-SearchBot` / `Disallow: /` and `User-agent: PerplexityBot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 75/100. I assumed you want to be found, since there is no `geo.config.json`. If the block is deliberate, set `policy.aiSearchCrawlers` in a `geo.config.json` to say so.

### 2. Give each page its own canonical URL
- **Why it matters:** A canonical tells search engines which address is the real one for a page. Yours says "the home page" for every page, so `/moorings` and `/contact` point away from themselves.
- **Where:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`
- **What the code says:** `<link rel="canonical" href="https://harbor.example/" />`
- **Size:** Small. Build the URL from `Astro.url.pathname` and the site origin.
- **Score after this:** 71/100

### 3. Fix the two broken structured-data blocks
- **Why it matters:** Structured data (JSON-LD) labels page facts for machines. Broken blocks get ignored.
- **Where:** `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`
- **What the code says:**
  - `" ": {` should be the key `acceptedAnswer`. The first FAQ question has no valid answer.
  - `"headline": "Moorings and prices", }` has a trailing comma, so it is invalid JSON.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 71/100. Fixing both GEO-004 problems earns the 2 points back, and the number shown is for fixing both.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt valid and reachable | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, plain valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have access | Problem | `public/robots.txt:4-8`, 0 of 3 points. Policy assumed. `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` aren't blocked. |
| GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Problem | `src/pages/contact.astro:4` is noindex yet listed in the sitemap. 2 of 3 routes clear, so 2 of 3 points. |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical per page | Problem | `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`, same URL on all 3 routes, 0 of 2 points |
| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Clear | Astro static pages, and `Newsletter` is server-rendered before hydration |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Problem | `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`, 0 of 2 points |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Clear | `public/sitemap.xml`, absolute `Sitemap:` line in `robots.txt:10` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Clear | `Base.astro:4,6,7`, and all 3 pages pass distinct values |
| GEO-016 | Server-rendered links | Clear | `Base.astro:12`, plain `<a href>` to all 3 routes |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits vs AI-search goal | Problem | `Base.astro:9`. `/` and `/moorings` inherit `max-snippet:0`, `/contact` doesn't. That's 1 of 3 routes clear, so 0.67 of 2 points. |
| GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | `Newsletter.jsx` (label and button text) and `Base.astro`. No images exist. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt | Not scored | Not present |
| GEO-102 | App structured data | Not scored | None |

## Other problems found

- **A noindex page is listed in the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:5` has `<loc>https://harbor.example/contact</loc>`, but `src/pages/contact.astro:4` sets `robots="noindex"`. Remove it from the sitemap, or drop the noindex.
- **A default that forbids snippets on every page:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:9` has `content={robots ?? "max-snippet:0"}`. It tells search and AI tools not to show text excerpts, which conflicts with wanting to be found. Default to `index, follow` instead. This is the cause of the GEO-017 result.

## Worth considering

- **Label the business:** `src/pages/contact.astro:6`: `Call the harbour office on 01326 000000.` Adding `LocalBusiness` or `Organization` JSON-LD with the name, phone and Falmouth location might help machines identify who you are. The `/contact` page is noindexed, so put it on the home page.
- **Give the home page real content:** `src/pages/index.astro:6-7` has a heading and one sentence, and its `<title>` and description duplicate the moorings topic. Add what the harbour is, where it is and how to book.
- **Add the facts the FAQ implies:** `src/data/faq.json:10,19` answer "by the night" and the "water taxi, May to September" visibly nowhere on the page. Rendering the Q&A as page text (not only JSON-LD) would make those facts readable.
- **Expand the prices page:** `src/pages/moorings.astro:7`: `Prices start at £40 a night.` Add sizes, seasonal rates and how to book, since the description promises "Mooring sizes and seasonal prices".
- **Add `<lastmod>`:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-5` has no dates. Add them if you know when each page changed.
- **Generate the sitemap:** The hand-kept `public/sitemap.xml` and the hardcoded origin could come from `@astrojs/sitemap`, with `site` set in Astro config (no `astro.config` file exists).
- **Add head basics and `<main>`:** `Base.astro:5-9` sets no `charset`, `viewport` or social tags, and the body has no `<main>`.
- **Link between pages:** Pages link onward only through the nav. A link from the prices text to the contact page would help readers.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. If you have an access log, `geopilot logs <access log>` checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live status codes and headers:** the server could add its own `X-Robots-Tag` headers, and I can't see those. A live scan would show them.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site (no `geo.config.json` was found). The blocker cap of 40 was not applied, because no policy was declared.
- `https://harbor.example` is the site's real origin.
- I read all 9 tracked files: the 3 routes, the layout, `Newsletter.jsx`, `faq.json`, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml` and `package.json`.
- Two JSON-LD sources exist (`faq.json` and the inline Article).

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
